question.en: A data set has mean \(\bar{x}=72\) and standard deviation \(s=8\). What \(z\)-score corresponds to \(x=88\)?

solution.en: \(z=(88-72)/8=2.0.\) The value 88 is exactly 2 standard deviations above the mean.
Strong positive linear association. \(r^2=0.7225.\) About 72.25% of the variability in \(y\) is explained by the linear relationship with \(x.\)

question.en: A 95% CI is \((47.2,\,52.8)\). Interpret it and state the margin of error.

solution.en: We are 95% confident the true mean lies between 47.2 and 52.8. MOE \(=(52.8-47.2)/2=2.8.\) Note: the mean is fixed — the interval is the random quantity.

question.en: Design a completely randomised experiment to test whether a new tutoring programme improves exam scores, using 60 volunteer students. Identify one potential confounding variable and explain how randomisation addresses it.

solution.en:
Number the 60 students 1–60. Use a random number generator to assign 30 to treatment (tutoring) and 30 to control (no tutoring). Compare mean exam scores after the programme.

Confounder: prior academic ability. Randomisation distributes prior ability roughly equally between groups on average, so the groups are comparable at baseline. The scope of inference is limited to volunteer students — results may not generalise to all students.
